Odds-ratio thresholds equivalent to d at a given baseline risk

Source: R/chen-or.R
chen_or_thresholds.Rd

Chen, Cohen & Chen (2010) translate Cohen's d into odds ratios by placing both groups on a latent normal scale. If p0 is the event risk in the reference (unexposed) group, a standardised difference d corresponds to an event risk in the exposed group of

Usage

chen_or_thresholds(
  baseline_risk,
  d = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8),
  labels = c("negligible", "small", "medium", "large")
)

Arguments

baseline_risk

Event risk in the reference group, strictly between 0 and 1.

d

Positive standardised differences that define the cut-points.

labels

Zone labels, one more than d.

Value

An es_thresholds() object with metric = "or", for use with geom_es_zones() and scale = "log".

Details

$$p_1 = \Phi(\Phi^{-1}(p_0) + d)$$

and the odds ratio is

$$OR = \frac{p_1 / (1 - p_1)}{p_0 / (1 - p_0)}.$$

This reproduces the published values: OR = 1.68, 3.47 and 6.71 for d = 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8 at p0 = 1%, and 1.52, 2.74 and 4.72 at p0 = 5%.

Why the zones are asymmetric

Under this model the odds ratio for a protective effect (d < 0) is not the reciprocal of the odds ratio for the same harmful effect, except at p0 = 0.5. At p0 = 1%, d = -0.8 corresponds to OR = 0.088 (1 / 11.4), not 1 / 6.71 = 0.149. chen_or_thresholds() therefore computes the boundaries below 1 from d < 0 directly (cuts_lower in es_thresholds()), rather than mirroring the boundaries above 1. Chen et al. tabulated only odds ratios above 1; the boundaries below 1 apply their method to negative d and are not published values.

p0 must be the risk in the group in the denominator of the odds ratio (the reference group of your estimates).

References

Chen H, Cohen P, Chen S (2010). How big is a big odds ratio? Interpreting the magnitudes of odds ratios in epidemiological studies. Communications in Statistics - Simulation and Computation 39(4):860-864. doi:10.1080/03610911003650383

See also

es_benchmarks() ("chen_or", the published 1% values)

Examples

chen_or_thresholds(0.01)
#> <es_thresholds> on the "or" scale
#> negligible (above null): magnitude in [1, 1.69)
#> small (above null): magnitude in [1.69, 3.47)
#> medium (above null): magnitude in [3.47, 6.71)
#> large (above null): magnitude in [6.71, Inf)
#> negligible (below null): magnitude in [1, 1.74)
#> small (below null): magnitude in [1.74, 4.28)
#> medium (below null): magnitude in [4.28, 11.4)
#> large (below null): magnitude in [11.4, Inf)
#> Source: Odds ratios equivalent to d = 0.2/0.5/0.8 at a 1% baseline risk, by the
#> method of Chen H, Cohen P, Chen S (2010). Commun Stat Simul Comput
#> 39(4):860-864, doi:10.1080/03610911003650383. Boundaries below 1 apply the
#> method to negative d.
chen_or_thresholds(0.20)
#> <es_thresholds> on the "or" scale
#> negligible (above null): magnitude in [1, 1.41)
#> small (above null): magnitude in [1.41, 2.31)
#> medium (above null): magnitude in [2.31, 3.74)
#> large (above null): magnitude in [3.74, Inf)
#> negligible (below null): magnitude in [1, 1.43)
#> small (below null): magnitude in [1.43, 2.53)
#> medium (below null): magnitude in [2.53, 4.72)
#> large (below null): magnitude in [4.72, Inf)
#> Source: Odds ratios equivalent to d = 0.2/0.5/0.8 at a 20% baseline risk, by
#> the method of Chen H, Cohen P, Chen S (2010). Commun Stat Simul Comput
#> 39(4):860-864, doi:10.1080/03610911003650383. Boundaries below 1 apply the
#> method to negative d.
